basic_info: Woman, late 30s, chief complaint: worsening headaches on the right side behind the eye, pulsing pain, associated with ringing in ears and occasional blurred vision
present_illness: Onset of headaches, progression to worsening, description of pain as pulsing on the right side behind the eye, associated symptoms of tinnitus and occasional blurred vision on the same side as the headache. The ringing in ears has been going on for a few months now, and the blurred vision is more recent—it comes and goes, usually on the same side as the headache. It doesn’t happen with every headache, but it’s been getting more frequent lately. It’s really worrying me. No nausea or vomiting with the headaches, and no photophobia. The only vision changes are the occasional blurred vision on the same side as the headache. The patient reports that the headaches worsen with stress and exercise. She has not experienced nausea, vomiting, or photophobia. She has not noticed any visual aura such as flashing lights or zigzag patterns prior to the headaches. She has not experienced any changes in her menstrual cycle or hormonal fluctuations that might be associated with the onset or worsening of her headaches. She has a history of headaches since her teenage years, which used to be around the time of her menstrual cycle, but have become more frequent and severe over time, and recently worsen with stress and exercise.
past_history: No history of migraines, trauma, or other neurological conditions reported.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, Temp 36.8°C. Neurological examination: no focal deficits, cranial nerves II-XII intact, no nystagmus, normal fundoscopy.
aux_exam: MRI brain (recent): no acute intracranial pathology. Visual field testing: no significant deficits. Audiogram: mild sensorineural hearing loss in the right ear. Lumbar puncture (if performed): normal opening pressure, CSF analysis unremarkable.
